companyDescription: Rare disease biotech · First-in-class inhaled MOLBREEVI (molgramostim) in Priority Review for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (aPAP) — no FDA-approved therapy exists for this ultra-rare lung disease today
priceNote: Trading near the top of its 52-week range ($1.98-$7.01), above its 200-day average, as buy-side positioning builds into the Nov 22 PDUFA
summary: Savara's MOLBREEVI has a PDUFA date of Nov 22, 2026 (extended 3 months from Aug 22 after the FDA requested additional information — no safety, efficacy, or manufacturing concerns were cited) to become the first and only approved therapy for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, an ultra-rare lung disease with real unmet need. Cash runway to H2 2027 removes near-term dilution risk, and Street consensus already prices in a meaningful probability of approval (avg target ~$9.20, high $16 vs a $5.69 current price). The binary is real: a clean approval could re-rate this as a first-in-class launch story, while a second delay or CRL — a genuine risk given the review has already slipped once — could cut the stock in half overnight.

catalysts.name: PDUFA decision — MOLBREEVI in autoimmune PAP
catalysts.description: FDA decides by Nov 22, 2026 whether to approve the first and only therapy for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis. Priority Review; no safety, efficacy, or manufacturing issues cited in the extension letter.

risks: CRL risk — review has already been extended once (Aug→Nov) after an FDA information request; a second delay or a Complete Response Letter is a real possibility despite no safety/efficacy issue cited
Small, thinly-traded rare-disease name — high headline volatility, plus dilution risk from capital raises to fund a commercial launch post-approval
Even on approval, aPAP is an ultra-rare, unfamiliar diagnosis for most pulmonologists — patient-finding and launch uptake could run slower than models assume

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held at 3.50-3.75% on Jul 29 with 3 hawkish dissents favoring a hike — rate-hike tail risk into year-end hasn't gone away
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE still 3.3% YoY, well above the 2% target
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Biotech is rate-sensitive as a long-duration, cash-burning sector, but SVRA's binary FDA catalyst dominates the stock's direction far more than macro does
macroRisk.summary: Macro risk is secondary here — the Nov 22 FDA decision, not the Fed, is what moves this stock

catalystSpot.preRunup: Rare-disease PDUFA names often drift up into the decision date as options positioning builds and buy-side conviction grows on a clean regulatory record — SVRA's Priority Review has no cited safety signal

postWin.range: +15% to +80% same-day/week; already-anticipated approvals can still add another +33% over the following month
postWin.note: Vera Therapeutics (Trutakna, Jul 2026) — already well-anticipated approval, +7% day-of but +33% over the next month as launch derisked. Underfollowed first-in-class rare-disease names can move far more explosively: Reata (Skyclarys, Feb 2023) jumped +199% the day after approval.

postLose.note: CRLs in rare-disease/orphan biotech have produced brutal single-day drops even without a cited safety issue — Corcept (CORT) fell -50% on a Dec 2025 CRL, RegenxBio (RGNX) fell -21% on a Feb 2026 CRL

spotSizing.reason: Binary FDA event with real precedent for -35% to -50% single-day downside on a miss; size small even given the first-in-class upside case

stopPreCatalyst.note: Below this, the clean pre-PDUFA setup is in question even before the FDA decision lands

stopPostCatalyst.note: If a CRL/delay hits, exit into the gap rather than average down — rare-disease CRLs have historically kept falling for days as the market re-prices the delay

comparableCases.note: Underfollowed first-in-class rare-disease approval — the stock nearly tripled overnight as the market re-rated a name few had modeled for a clean approval.
Already well-anticipated approval — modest +7% day-of pop, but the stock re-rated +33% over the following month as commercial launch derisked.
A CRL with no cited safety issue still triggered a 50% single-day collapse — shows how violently binary FDA misses can move even a well-covered name.
